title: Mouse kidney nuclear isolation and library preparation for single-cell combinatorial indexing RNA sequencing
protocol: Prepare materials and equipment for nuclei extraction.
Prepare NLB1 buffer according to the recipe provided below.
Place the prepared NLB1 buffer on ice.
Add one tablet of cOmplete Mini Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (EDTA-free) to 10 mL Nuclei EZ Lysis Buffer.
Ensure the protease inhibitor tablet is completely dissolved by gentle vortexing at room temperature for 10-15 minutes.
Prepare NLB2 buffer according to the recipe provided below.
Place the prepared NLB2 buffer on ice.
Clean the dounce tissue grinder and both pestles with RNaseZap Decontamination Solution.
Wash the cleaned equipment with RNase-free water.
Prepare Nuclei Isolation Buffer with the provided recipe.
Place the prepared buffer on ice.
Prepare a 4% paraformaldehyde solution and place it on ice.
Precool a 6-cm dish, a razor blade, a 200-μm cell strainer, a 40-μm cell strainer, and several 15-mL and 50-mL centrifuge tubes in the 4°C cold room.
Thaw the kidney tissue stored at −80°C and immediately transfer it to the pre-cooled 6-cm dish.
Add 2 mL of NLB1 to the dish containing the thawed tissue.
Mince the tissue thoroughly with a razor blade to avoid big chunks.
Transfer 1–1.5 mL tissue suspension into the dounce grinder.
Move the small grinder pestle up and down for 15 times to induce cell dissociation.
Transfer homogenates in the dounce grinder onto a 200-μm cell strainer laid on a 50-mL centrifuge tube.
Repeat grinding with the large grinder pestle (tight pestle) up and down for 5 times for further nuclear dissociation.
Transfer the nuclei suspension to a 15-mL centrifuge tube.
Add another 1 mL NLB1 to the nuclei suspension.
Incubate for 5 min.
Filter the nuclei suspension with a 40-μm cell strainer.
Spin down the nuclei by centrifugation at 500 g for 4 min at 4°C.
Use a refrigerated centrifuge with a swinging bucket to increase nuclei yield.
Remove supernatant and resuspend the nuclei pellet with 1.5 mL NLB2 by pipetting 10 times.
Mix the nuclei suspension with the rest of NLB2 and incubate for 5 min.
Spin down the nuclei by centrifugation at 500 g for 4 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant thoroughly and resuspend the nuclei with 2 mL NIB.
Count the number of fresh nuclei, aiming to extract at least 15 million nuclei from a kidney tissue of 100 mg.
Add 3 ml ice-cold 4% PFA to the 2 ml nuclei suspension for a final concentration of 2.4%.
Mix thoroughly by inverting the tube for 3 times.
Fix the nuclei on ice for 10 minutes.
Spin down the fixed nuclei by centrifugation at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and wash with 2 mL NIB.
Resuspend the nuclei pellet with 300 μL NIB.
Count the number of nuclei.
Dilute the nuclei with NIB to a final concentration of 5–10 million/mL.
Aliquot the nuclei suspension to several cryogenic tubes with 300 μL materials per tube.
Flash freeze the nuclei suspension with liquid nitrogen.
Store the sample in a liquid nitrogen tank for future sci-RNA-seq3 processing.
Prepare all reagents and equipment ahead and precool in a 4°C cold room before performing nuclei isolation on mouse kidney tissue.
Transfer a frozen mouse kidney tissue onto a 6-cm dish.
Mince the mouse kidney tissue with a razor blade in NLB1 buffer.
Prepare 35 mL NIB buffer and place on ice.
Prepare Nuclei Buffer with BSA (NBB) and place on ice.
Prepare permeabilization buffer and place on ice.
Take one vial of fixed nuclei in a cryogenic tube (300 μL) out of the liquid nitrogen tank for each sample.
Thaw all samples in a 37°C water bath for 30–60 seconds.
Immediately place thawed samples on ice after removal from the water bath.
Transfer the nuclei suspension into a 15-mL centrifuge tube for each sample.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C to spin down the nuclei of all samples.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet thoroughly with 100 μL NIB.
Add 400 μL permeabilization buffer to each sample.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C to spin down the nuclei.
Carefully remove the supernatant from each sample.
Resuspend the pellet with 250 μL NIB and transfer into a 1.5 mL tube for each sample.
Place the 1.5 mL tubes in a Bioruptor Pico Sonication device.
Perform sonication for 10 seconds using the Bioruptor Pico.
Filter the nuclei suspension through a 40-μm Flowmi cell strainer for each sample.
Keep samples on ice after filtration.
Measure and record the concentration of nuclei for each sample.
Dilute each sample to approximately 3.6 × 10^6 nuclei/mL with NIB.
Thaw the four 96-well plates prepared ahead of time for reverse transcription.
Centrifuge the plates briefly.
Add 2 μL dNTP (10 mM) into each of the 384 wells.
Centrifuge the plates briefly.
Record the well positions where nuclei from each sample are deposited.
Add around 80,000 nuclei (in 22 μL suspension) into each of the 384 wells to the bottom.
Incubate the four plates at 55°C for 5 minutes.
Place the plates on ice immediately after incubation.
Prepare reverse transcription reaction mix according to the provided recipe.
Distribute 14 μL reaction mix into each well using a multichannel pipette.
Place plates on ice.
Add 60 μL NBB into each well with a multichannel pipette to dilute the nuclei suspension.
Pool the nuclei suspension from all 384 wells together into a reservoir.
Split the pooled nuclei suspension into two 50-mL tubes.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 10 min at 4°C and remove supernatant carefully.
Thaw four 96-well plates for hairpin ligation prepared ahead of time.
Briefly centrifuge the thawed plates.
Prepare ligation reaction mix according to provided recipe.
Distribute 22 μL reaction mix into each of the 384 wells with a multichannel pipette.
Resuspend nuclei pellet from step 6.k with 4.3 mL NIB thoroughly.
Distribute 10 μL nuclei suspension into each of the 384 wells with a multichannel pipette.
Perform ligation reaction by incubating plates at 25°C for 10 min.
Add 60 μL NBB into each well with a multichannel pipette to dilute the nuclei suspension after reaction.
Pool the diluted nuclei suspension from all 384 wells together into a reservoir.
Split pooled nuclei suspension into two 50-mL tubes and add another 20 mL NBB to each tube.
Centrifuge at 600 g for 10 min and remove supernatant.
Resuspend the nuclei pellet with 2.5 mL NBB.
Combine all resuspended pellets into a single 15-mL tube.
Centrifuge at 600 g for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the nuclei pellet with 4 mL NBB.
Filter the nuclei suspension through 40-μm Flowmi cell strainers.
Determine the concentration of nuclei using an automated cell counter or a hemacytometer.
Dilute the nuclei suspension to achieve a concentration of 600–800 nuclei/μL with NBB.
Distribute 5 μL of nuclei suspension (3,000–4,000 nuclei) into each well of several 96-well plates.
Seal the plates.
Briefly centrifuge the sealed plates.
Resuspend lyophilized ME_REV and ME_A oligos to a stock concentration of 100 μM using Annealing Buffer.
Mix 5 μL of ME_REV (100 μM) with 10 μL of ME_A (100 μM) in a PCR tube.
Briefly spin down the mixture.
Add 10 μL naked Tn5 transposase to 12.5 μL annealed oligos generated above.
Mix well and briefly centrifuge the tube.
Incubate the Tn5-oligo mix at 23°C for 30–40 min.
Supplement the suspension with 12.5 μL glycerol and mix well.
Thaw one 96-well plate generated in step 7.s at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Briefly centrifuge the plate.
Prepare second-strand synthesis reaction mix with recipe provided below.
Distribute 5 μL second-strand synthesis reaction mix into each of the 96 wells with a multichannel pipette.
Vortex and briefly centrifuge the plate.
Seal the plate and perform second-strand synthesis at 16°C for 3 h.
Dilute 2 μL of oligo-loaded Tn5 transposome to a final concentration of 100 nM using Tagmentation Buffer.
Further dilute the 100 nM transposome with Tagmentation Buffer to achieve the working concentration.
Vortex and briefly centrifuge the plate after the reaction in step 9.e.
Place the plate on ice.
Add 10 μL of Tn5 transposome at the working concentration into each of the 96 wells using a multichannel pipette.
Incubate the plate at 55°C for 5 min.
Add 20 μL DNA binding buffer to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Vortex and briefly centrifuge the plate.
Incubate the plate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 5 minutes and then briefly centrifuge the plate.
Place the plate on a magnet for 5 minutes, then carefully remove supernatant.
Add 40 μL AMPure XP beads to each well with a multichannel pipette and mix well.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 5 minutes and then briefly centrifuge the plate.
Place the plate on a magnet for 1 minute, then carefully remove supernatant.
Wash each well with 100 μL 80% ethanol using a multichannel pipette while keeping the plate on the magnet.
Incubate for 30 seconds and then remove supernatant.
Repeat steps 11.a.iv–11.a.v for the second wash.
Remove the plate from the magnet and place it at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 5 minutes to let residual ethanol evaporate.
Prepare USER reaction mix with recipe provided below.
Add 10 μL USER reaction mix to each well containing beads only using a multichannel pipette.
Mix the beads with USER reaction mix by pipetting for 10–20 times.
Seal the plate and incubate the plate at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Vortex and briefly centrifuge the plate.
Add 7 μL Elution buffer to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Vortex and briefly centrifuge the plate.
Place the plate on the magnet for 5 minutes.
Transfer 16 μL supernatant of each well to a new 96-well plate.
Briefly centrifuge the new plate.
Place the new plate on ice.
Add 2 μL uniquely indexed P5 primers (10 μM) into each well.
Add 2 μL uniquely indexed P7 primers (10 μM) into each well.
Incubate the plate at 80°C for 10 min.
Add 20 μL NEBNext High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix into each well.
Briefly centrifuge the plate.
Start the PCR reaction.
Pool PCR products from all 96 wells together in a 15-mL tube.
Thaw pooled PCR products and transfer 900 μl to a 2-ml tube.
Perform library purification with 0.8× Select-a-Size MagBeads.
Add 720 μl beads and mix thoroughly.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 5 min.
Separate the beads by placing the tube against a magnet for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and wash the beads twice with 200 μl 80% ethanol while keeping the tube on the magnet.
Carefully remove all ethanol and air dry for 3–5 min.
Remove the tube from the magnet.
Add 100 μl Elution buffer and mix with the beads thoroughly.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 3–5 minutes.
Place the tube on the magnet for 3 minutes to separate the beads.
Transfer all supernatant carefully to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Add 70 μL beads and repeat procedures of step 13.b.
Elute the sub-library with 20 μL Elution buffer.
Store the sub-library at −20°C for several months if needed.
Visualize the sub-library on a Bioanalyzer or Tapestation instrument.
Determine the concentration of the sub-library.
Balance all sub-libraries to the same molarity.
Pool all sub-libraries together.
Sequence on a NovaSeq 6000 platform (Read1-Index1-Index2-Read2: 34-10-10-100 bp).
Test four different concentrations of Tn5 transposome when processing the first 96-well plate for sci-RNA-seq sub-library generation, with 24 wells per condition.
Pool PCR products from 24 wells and process them for sub-library generation after steps 10–12.
Visualize and quantify the four sub-libraries created.
Choose the sub-library with the highest concentration to determine the working concentration of Tn5 transposome.
Perform nuclei isolation and fixation from one mouse kidney tissue following steps 1–3.
Prepare 4 mL NIB, 4 mL NBB, and 400 μL permeabilization buffer at step 4.
Perform nuclei permeabilization on fixed nuclei generated from the tissue of use following step 5.
Distribute the nuclei suspension into 10 wells of a 96-well plate for reverse transcription.
Add a uniquely indexed RT oligo into each of the 10 wells.
Prepare 154 μL reverse transcription reaction mix and follow the other procedures of step 6 accordingly.
Distribute the nuclei suspension into 10 wells of a 96-well plate for hairpin ligation.
Add a uniquely ligation oligo into each of the 10 wells.
Prepare 231 μL ligation reaction mix.
Distribute nuclei suspension to at least 20 wells of a 96-well plate (3,000–4,000 nuclei in 5 μL per well).
Use Tn5 transposome as a final concentration of 10 nM for tagmentation.
Add 20 different P5/P7 primer combinations to the 20 wells.
Set PCR cycling number to 16.
Process approximately 800 μL PCR products.
Sequence the library on a MiSeq platform or with a spike-in approach (Read1-Index1-Index2-Read2: 34-10-10-100 bp).
